# Brief: reference-impl v0.6.3 — walker friction patches from the v0.6.2 dogfood

The v0.6.2 release shipped 2026-04-27 (Plan CLV-45, 4 tasks merged, final
HEAD `b472605`). The walker run that produced it surfaced three concrete
pain points that cost real time during the run, plus one ship-discipline
gap discovered at npm-publish time. None require an architectural lift;
all four are ~small, well-scoped edits in the walker / prep-worktree /
publish surfaces.

This brief drives v0.6.3: a focused patch line that closes the v0.6.2
debt, one more turn of the dogfood crank before any v0.7 design work.

## Goal

Ship `@cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.3` with four small fixes that make
the walker's per-task Session B lifecycle and the post-walker release
flow reliable end-to-end. Standard stays at 0.4.1. No new tracks, no new
agents.

## Background

Source: the v0.6.2 walker run on Plan CLV-45 (this very session). All
four items were observed live during the run; no separate dogfood
debrief is needed beyond this brief. The CHANGELOG.md `merge=union` fix
(CLV-47) means parallel Documenter entries no longer conflict, so v0.6.3
can have multiple non-custodian Documenters writing `## [Unreleased]`
bullets without coordination — that simplifies this Plan's DAG vs. v0.6.2.

## In-scope bug fixes

Each item below is a candidate task. The Plan agent decides task
granularity; suggested topology is at the bottom.

1. **`cloverleaf-cli prep-worktree` does not build `reference-impl/dist`.**
   The CLV-37 (v0.6.1) walk-up logic ensures `mainRoot` resolves to the
   primary repo, and `prep-worktree` then runs `npm run build` inside
   the worktree's `standard/`. But it never builds `reference-impl/`
   itself. Reviewer / QA agents that import from
   `<worktree>/reference-impl/dist/lib/qa-report.js` (and similar) hit
   `Cannot find module` errors and stall.
   In the v0.6.2 walker run, every Session B (CLV-46, CLV-47, CLV-48,
   CLV-49) hit this. The recovery pattern was a manual
   `cp -a /home/ren/Workspace/cloverleaf/reference-impl/dist
   <worktree>/reference-impl/dist` per session.
   Fix: extend `lib/prep-worktree.ts` to either (a) `cp` primary's
   `reference-impl/dist` into the worktree, or (b) run
   `npm run build` inside the worktree's `reference-impl/` after the
   node_modules copy. Preferred: (a), to avoid double-build cost on
   every Session B spawn (the primary's dist is already correct for
   the current main HEAD).

2. **Session B repeatedly attempts `git checkout main` from inside a
   walker worktree.** Two of the v0.6.2 walker sessions (CLV-46 and
   CLV-49) tried `git checkout main` mid-task. Each time main is held
   by the primary repo, so the checkout fails — but the failure costs
   wall-time and recovery turns. CLV-48's CWD-preflight fix anchors
   each agent to the worktree root via `cd "$(git rev-parse
   --show-toplevel)"` but does NOT prevent a session from attempting
   to switch branches.
   Fix: (a) add an explicit "DO NOT `git checkout main` from this
   worktree — main is held by the primary repo. To compare against
   main, use `git diff main..HEAD` or `git worktree add --detach
   /tmp/<dir> main`" line to the walker `SKILL.md` scenario_brief
   template; AND/OR (b) ship a default starter policy fragment in the
   walker that auto-rejects `^git checkout main\b` in walker worktrees.
   Both are SKILL.md / prompt-text edits, no code change.

3. **`prepublishOnly` fails opaquely when primary's `standard/` isn't
   prepped.** During the v0.6.1 retroactive publish today, `npm publish`
   from `/tmp/publish-v0.6.1/reference-impl` failed inside
   `prepublishOnly` (which runs `npm test && npm run build`) because
   the worktree's `standard/` had no `dist/` and no `node_modules/`.
   The error was a vitest/tsc module-resolution failure, not a
   helpful "you need to prep first" message.
   Fix: add a pre-test sanity check in `reference-impl/scripts/`
   (called from `prepublishOnly` or directly from the `test` script)
   that `existsSync` checks `<repoRoot>/standard/dist/` and
   `<repoRoot>/standard/node_modules/`, and exits non-zero with a
   clear "run `cloverleaf-cli prep-worktree <primaryRoot> <worktree>`
   first, OR `(cd ../standard && npm ci && npm run build)`" message.
   Pure error-message improvement; no functional behavior change.

4. **No post-walker release reminder.** When the walker drains the
   final-gate queue and prints `✓ Plan <PLAN-ID> complete`, it gives
   no further guidance. The release-prep custodian task already bumps
   `package.json` and renames the CHANGELOG section, so the merge to
   main is "shippable", but the operator still has to remember to
   `git tag`, `git push`, `npm publish`, and `gh release create`.
   v0.6.1 shipped to local main only because of exactly this gap —
   the walker drained successfully, the operator moved on, and no
   reminder fired.
   Fix: extend the walker `SKILL.md` step-6 (Report) to print an
   explicit `Next steps` block when `every task in the plan's
   task_dag.nodes has state: "merged"`, listing the four remaining
   commands (`git tag -a`, `git push origin main`, `git push origin
   <tag>`, `cd reference-impl && npm publish --access public`,
   `gh release create`). Optionally surface them as a structured
   payload that a future `/cloverleaf-release` skill can consume.
   Smallest-viable: SKILL.md prose addition.

## Open questions / Discovery hooks

1. **#1 prep-worktree fix mechanism.** Copy primary's `dist` (cheap,
   fast, exactly mirrors current main HEAD) vs. fresh build in the
   worktree (correct for branches that touch `lib/` but doubles the
   spawn cost on every Session B). Recommend (a) copy. Spike worth it?
   Probably not — choice is obvious.

2. **#2 default-policy enforcement vs. prompt-text.** The starter
   policy claw-drive ships is generic; cloverleaf doesn't currently
   ship a policy template. If the walker injected a policy fragment
   for `^git checkout main` rejection, that would be more enforceable
   than a prompt instruction. But the operator already passes a
   policy at `start_session` time. Adding a "you must include this
   pattern" requirement is a contract on the operator, not the
   walker. Probably better to do (a) prompt-text only and document
   (b) as a recommended addition to the operator's policy template.

3. **#4 inline reminder vs. separate `/cloverleaf-release` skill.**
   The minimal-viable is a SKILL.md prose addition. The richer path
   is a new `/cloverleaf-release` skill that the walker invokes (or
   the operator runs manually post-walker) which: tags at HEAD, pushes
   main + tag, runs `npm publish` from the right cwd, and creates the
   GitHub Release. The richer path is more useful but is its own task.
   Recommend prose-only for v0.6.3; defer the skill to v0.7 or v0.6.4.

The Plan agent doesn't need spikes for these — answers are above.

## Parallel-DAG conflict guidance

Files this release will touch:

- `reference-impl/lib/prep-worktree.ts` — fix #1 only.
- `reference-impl/skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md` — fixes #2 AND
  #4 (both are SKILL.md prose edits). Combine into a single task to
  avoid file overlap.
- `reference-impl/scripts/` (new file probably) + `reference-impl/package.json`
  (`prepublishOnly` script tweak) — fix #3.
- `reference-impl/tests/` — new regression tests per fix.
- `reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md` — release-prep custodian only writes
  the `## 0.6.3` header rename. **Crucially, with v0.6.2's `merge=union`
  in place, non-custodian Documenters CAN add `## [Unreleased]` bullets
  without conflicting** — that's the exact scenario v0.6.2 set up.
  No suppression logic needed.
- `reference-impl/package.json` — version-bump custodian only writes
  the `0.6.2` → `0.6.3` change.

## Success criteria

- `prep-worktree` produces a worktree where `<worktree>/reference-impl/dist/`
  is present and matches primary's dist. Regression test in
  `reference-impl/tests/`.
- Walker `SKILL.md` scenario_brief includes an explicit "DO NOT git
  checkout main" instruction. Regression test asserts the string
  appears.
- `prepublishOnly` (or its preceding sanity check) prints a helpful
  error message when run from a worktree where `standard/dist/` or
  `standard/node_modules/` is absent. Regression test that simulates
  a missing-standard worktree and asserts the helpful message.
- Walker `SKILL.md` step-6 emits a `Next steps` block (tag / push /
  npm publish / gh release) when the plan completes. Regression test
  asserts the section appears in the SKILL.md template.
- v0.6.3 release dogfood completes without manual `cp -a dist`,
  without `git checkout main` attempts, and with the operator
  prompted at the right moment to run the post-merge sequence.
- `reference-impl/package.json` is `0.6.3`.
- `reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md` has a `## 0.6.3` section listing the
  four fixes.
- Tag `reference-impl-v0.6.3` pushed; GitHub Release live; npm publish
  done.

## Non-goals

- New `/cloverleaf-release` skill that automates the post-merge
  sequence. Defer to v0.6.4 or v0.7 (the v0.6.3 fix prints commands;
  it does not run them).
- DAG-edge inference from shared-file overlap (v0.7 design).
- Unified `/cloverleaf-flow` orchestrator (v0.7).
- Standard schema, contract, or conformance changes (stays at 0.4.1).
- Walker external API changes — skill name, args, exit behavior
  unchanged. Only SKILL.md prose, lib/, scripts/, package.json change.
- Retroactively fixing v0.6.0/0.6.1/0.6.2 — those are merged + tagged
  + published; v0.6.3 stands forward.
solution:
Four focused bug fixes ship as `@cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.3` with no Standard changes (stays at 0.4.1) and no new vocabulary, agents, tracks, or external API surface. The walker's skill name, invocation arguments, and exit behavior are unchanged. Three fixes run as parallel root tasks (T1, T2, T3) converging into a release-prep join sink (T4).

**Fix #1 — prep-worktree does not copy reference-impl/dist (`lib/prep-worktree.ts`).**
Extend `prepWorktree()` in `reference-impl/lib/prep-worktree.ts` to copy the primary repo's `reference-impl/dist` into the worktree after the existing `node_modules` copy step. Concretely, add a `primeCopy(join(resolvedMain, 'reference-impl', 'dist'), join(worktreePath, 'reference-impl', 'dist'))` call immediately after `primeCopy(mainRefImplNm, wtRefImplNm)`. Option (a) — copy primary's dist — is preferred over option (b) — fresh build in the worktree: it avoids the double-build cost on every Session B spawn, and primary's dist is already correct for current main HEAD, which is exactly the base any task branch was cut from at spawn time. The `primeCopy` helper already handles idempotence (wipe then copy) and verbatim symlinks, so no new machinery is needed. A regression test in the existing `reference-impl/tests/prep-worktree.test.ts` adds a case asserting that `<worktree>/reference-impl/dist/` is present and contains at least one `.mjs` file after `prepWorktree()` runs against a fixture primary.

**Fix #2 — Session B git checkout main guard + Fix #4 — post-walker release reminder (`SKILL.md`).**
Fixes #2 and #4 both modify `reference-impl/skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md` and are delivered by a single task (T2) to prevent parallel-DAG file overlap.

For fix #2: Insert an explicit warning paragraph into the Session B scenario_brief template in SKILL.md: "DO NOT run `git checkout main` from this worktree. The `main` branch is already checked out in the primary repo; a worktree cannot check out a branch that is held elsewhere and the command will fail. To compare against main, use `git diff main..HEAD`. To inspect main's content at a specific path, use `git show main:<path>`." This is a prose-text edit only; no policy or code change. Prompt-text (option a) is sufficient and avoids adding an operator-level policy contract. A regression test asserts the sentinel phrase "DO NOT" (or the specific text) appears in the SKILL.md scenario_brief section.

For fix #4: Extend SKILL.md step-6 (Report) with a conditional `## Next steps` block. When the walker's final report finds every task in the plan's `task_dag.nodes` with `state: "merged"`, the Report section prints the following block (where `<VERSION>` is read from `reference-impl/package.json`):
```
## Next steps (release publishing)
git tag -a reference-impl-v<VERSION> -m "reference-impl v<VERSION>"
git push origin main
git push origin reference-impl-v<VERSION>
(cd reference-impl && npm publish --access public)
gh release create reference-impl-v<VERSION> --title "reference-impl v<VERSION>" --notes-from-tag
```
This is a SKILL.md prose addition only. The `/cloverleaf-release` skill that automates these commands is deferred to v0.6.4 or v0.7; the block is structured to be consumable by such a skill in a future iteration. A regression test asserts the `## Next steps` section (or the sentinel command `git tag -a`) appears in the SKILL.md Report step.

**Fix #3 — prepublishOnly opaque failure (`scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` + `package.json`).**
Add a new script `reference-impl/scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` that: (1) walks up from `process.cwd()` to locate the repo root by detecting `standard/package.json`; (2) calls `existsSync` on `<repoRoot>/standard/dist/` and `<repoRoot>/standard/node_modules/`; (3) if either is absent, prints to stderr:
```
ERROR: standard/ is not prepped in this environment.
Run:  cloverleaf-cli prep-worktree <primaryRoot> <worktreeRoot>
  OR: (cd ../standard && npm ci && npm run build)
```
and exits non-zero. Update `reference-impl/package.json` `prepublishOnly` from `"npm test && npm run build"` to `"node scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs && npm test && npm run build"` so the sanity check fires before the expensive vitest/tsc run, giving immediate actionable feedback instead of a cryptic module-resolution failure. A regression test in `reference-impl/tests/` simulates a worktree environment without `standard/dist/` and `standard/node_modules/`, imports or spawns the script, and asserts the helpful error message appears in stderr with a non-zero exit code.

**DAG topology.**
Three parallel root tasks — (T1) prep-worktree dist copy, touching `lib/prep-worktree.ts` and the existing `tests/prep-worktree.test.ts`; (T2) SKILL.md prose edits (fix #2 + fix #4), touching `skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md` and a new SKILL.md regression test; (T3) prepublishOnly sanity check, touching `scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` [new] and `package.json` [prepublishOnly script line update] and a new test — converge into (T4) a release-prep join-sink task. T4 is the sole custodian of `reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md` (renames `## [Unreleased]` to `## 0.6.3` with date, normalizes bullet order) and the `version` field in `reference-impl/package.json` (`0.6.2 → 0.6.3`). T3 → T4 is a required DAG edge because both touch `package.json`; T1 and T2 have no shared-file overlap with each other or with T3. With v0.6.2's `.gitattributes` `merge=union` rule in place, non-custodian Documenters can append `## [Unreleased]` bullets during T1/T2/T3 delivery without conflict; T4 normalizes the final section at release-prep time.
acceptance_criteria: `prepWorktree()` in `lib/prep-worktree.ts` copies `<primary>/reference-impl/dist` into `<worktree>/reference-impl/dist` immediately after the `reference-impl/node_modules` copy. Regression test in `tests/prep-worktree.test.ts` verifies `<worktree>/reference-impl/dist/` exists and contains at least one `.mjs` file after `prepWorktree()` runs.

Walker `SKILL.md` scenario_brief template contains an explicit 'DO NOT run `git checkout main` from this worktree' instruction with safe alternatives (`git diff main..HEAD`, `git show main:<path>`). Regression test asserts the sentinel phrase appears in the SKILL.md scenario_brief section.

`reference-impl/scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` exists and exits non-zero with a clear human-readable message ('standard/ is not prepped') when `standard/dist/` or `standard/node_modules/` is absent from the repo root. Regression test simulates a missing-standard environment and asserts the helpful error message in stderr and non-zero exit code.

`reference-impl/package.json` `prepublishOnly` invokes `node scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` before `npm test`, so an unprepped worktree produces the actionable error immediately without running the full vitest/tsc suite.

Walker `SKILL.md` step-6 (Report) contains a `## Next steps` block listing the five post-merge release commands (git tag -a, git push origin main, git push origin <tag>, npm publish, gh release create) when every plan task is merged. Regression test asserts the section is present in the template.

`reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md` has a `## 0.6.3` section (renamed from `## [Unreleased]` by the T4 release-prep custodian) listing all four fixes: prep-worktree dist copy, git checkout main guard, prepublishOnly sanity check, and post-walker release reminder.

Tag `reference-impl-v0.6.3` is created at the merge commit, pushed to origin, a GitHub Release is published with a summary of the four fixes, and `@cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.3` is published to npm.

The v0.6.3 delivery dogfood completes without any manual `cp -a dist` recovery steps, without `git checkout main` failures in any Session B, and with the operator receiving the post-merge `## Next steps` release sequence automatically at plan completion.
out_of_scope: New `/cloverleaf-release` skill automating the post-merge release sequence (tag, push, npm publish, gh release create). Deferred to v0.6.4 or v0.7; v0.6.3 prints the commands but does not execute them.

Policy-fragment enforcement for `git checkout main` rejection in walker worktrees (option b from the brief). Deferred as a recommended addition to the operator's policy template; this RFC delivers prompt-text only (option a).
DAG-edge inference from shared-file modification overlap. Deferred to v0.7 design; the v0.6.3 Plan itself relies on file-overlap guidance encoded in this RFC.
Unified `/cloverleaf-flow` orchestrator fusing Discovery and Delivery. Deferred to v0.7 scope.
Changes to `@cloverleaf/standard` schemas, contracts, or conformance harness — Standard stays at 0.4.1 and its `package.json` is not touched.
Walker external API changes — skill name, invocation arguments, and exit behavior are unchanged. Only SKILL.md prose, `lib/prep-worktree.ts`, `scripts/`, and `package.json` change.
Retroactively amending v0.6.0, v0.6.1, or v0.6.2 — those versions are merged, tagged, and published; v0.6.3 stands forward.
